purpose: library: global atmospheric circulation as an ordered system — the no-rotation, no-water thought experiment (equatorial heating, rising air, a constant low-pressure belt, poleward return flow) and why Earth's rotation (the Coriolis effect) and land/water distribution break it into three circulation cells per hemisphere: 1. Hadley cell (low latitudes; George Hadley, 1735), 2. Ferrel cell (mid-latitudes; William Ferrell, 1856; the westerlies between 35° and 60° N/S), 3. Polar cell (high latitudes; sinking air over the poles forming high pressure). Fits step ordering of the circulation sequence, a compare table of the three cells (latitude band × flow × history), quiz cards with predict-then-reveal on the dates and latitude bands, and a concept map.
